course_name_en: Selected Subjects of Thermal Energy Technology

learning_outcomes.text: Students will have detailed knowledge of the concepts for providing, transporting and storing thermal energy, as well as its possible uses and limitations. They can compare the essential components of these systems, calculate the processes and evaluate optimization possibilities. They are able to distinguish individual components of a thermal system and make evidence-based, qualitative and quantitative judgments about their use.

Students analyze technical problems and develop solutions. This may also involve computer-aided calculation methods. Students apply common calculation methods to evaluate the results and are able to implement the underlying material data, tables and diagrams in their planning. Students can describe thermal engineering problems, develop solutions and implement them computationally. Graduates of the module realize tasks within the framework of municipal heating planning and thus transfer the content into real implementation scenarios.

Students know essential constellations of heat supply and distribution systems and are able to evaluate them with regard to possible applications and their efficiency. They can assess the potential of existing (waste) heat sources and their use as heating or process energies and design suitable systems. Students are able to interpret currently necessary adjustments to heat supply. Students understand the different methods for providing, distributing or transporting, storing and using thermal energy and select the appropriate method for the respective application. With regard to the different and diverse projects for municipal heat planning, graduates contribute to the implementation of the diverse solution options.

Students present the results obtained by calculation in a written report. They can present and discuss issues of thermal systems. They are competent discussion partners for questions from the field of thermal energy technology and the heat transition.

Students understand the different boundary conditions for the analysis of technical systems for the use and provision of thermal energy, energy conversion and thermal energy transport. They evaluate suitable processes, components and procedures and appropriate applications with regard to technical and societal challenges, develop solution approaches and justify their implementation.

syllabus_topics: Sector coupling in heating and cooling technology
Planning and simulation for energy and heat supply concepts
Power to X and hydrogen applications
assessment_rules: The graded examination is a written exam, duration as per the valid study regulations. The ungraded examination is experimental work consisting of 2 experiments.
